findings.title: Client-supplied edge headers reset the rate-limit bucket, removing all brute-force protection on login and admin login
findings.exploitability: Unauthenticated, remote, deterministic, no user interaction
findings.impact: Unlimited credential guessing against POST /api/admin/login (nominal 5/15min) and POST /api/auth/login (nominal 20/15min); admin compromise grants full analytics/PII dashboard access
findings.evidence: 40 admin-login attempts with rotating cf-connecting-ip returned 401 with X-RateLimit-Remaining=4 (bucket reset every request); identical run with a fixed header returned 429
findings.remediation: Added apps/server/src/client-address.ts: resolve the client address from a configured trusted-proxy hop count, counting X-Forwarded-For from the right; honour CF-Connecting-IP only when TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true; fall back to the socket address rather than a constant string
regressionTests: apps/server/src/security-controls.test.ts :: spoofed cf-connecting-ip cannot reset the admin-login rate limit
apps/server/src/security-controls.test.ts :: spoofed x-forwarded-for cannot reset the login rate limit
findings.residualRisk: TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS must match the real deployment. If the origin is reachable directly, bypassing Traefik, a forged single-entry XFF is still accepted; restrict origin ingress to the proxy at the network layer.

findings.title: sharp 0.33.5 carries unpatched libvips CVEs and is reached with attacker-supplied image bytes

cvss4.note: Upstream GHSA reports no numeric score; rated High on reachability with attacker-controlled decoder input

findings.exploitability: Requires an authenticated account (self-registration is open); decoder reached before any format allowlist check
findings.impact: Memory-safety defects in libvips decoders processing untrusted images
findings.confidence: High for reachability; upstream advisory for the defect itself
findings.remediation: Upgraded sharp 0.33.5 -> 0.35.4 in apps/server and apps/app
findings.residualRisk: sharp 0.35.4 requires Node >=20.9.0 while root engines still says >=20; the shipped container uses oven/bun so this affects only non-container Node runs.

findings.title: Analytics client IP taken from the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry, which any client can forge
findings.impact: Forged source IPs and geolocations stored in analytics_sessions, surfaced on the admin map/sessions views, and used to select IPs for paid MaxMind Insights lookups. Directly contradicted the rate-limiter, which read the opposite end of the same header.
findings.confidence: High - by inspection; the leftmost entry is definitionally client-supplied
findings.remediation: clientIp() now delegates to the shared resolveClientAddress() with the same trusted-hop rule as the rate limiter
findings.residualRisk: Same deployment dependency on TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS as LC-SEC-001.

findings.title: Container image runs the server as root
findings.location: Dockerfile:29-54 (runtime stage had no USER directive)
findings.attackerControlledInput: n/a - severity multiplier for any RCE, notably the libvips path in LC-SEC-002
findings.exploitability: Not independently exploitable; removes a containment boundary
findings.impact: Any code execution in the server process would run as uid 0, with write access to the whole image and the mounted litechat-data volume
findings.remediation: Runtime stage now chowns /app to the image's existing bun user (uid/gid 1000) and sets USER bun; docker-compose pins user 1000:1000 so the data volume is owned correctly
regressionTests: Not unit-testable; requires a container build (docker unavailable on the audit host)
findings.residualRisk: Existing deployments have a root-owned litechat-data volume and need a one-time chown -R 1000:1000; unverified because no Docker runtime was available.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy on any response
findings.exploitability: No injection sink was found in any client (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/eval anywhere in 175 source files), so there is nothing to exploit today
findings.impact: A future DOM-injection bug would have had no second line of defence; framing was only blocked by the legacy X-Frame-Options header
findings.remediation: Explicit CSP configured on secureHeaders(): default-src 'self', object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'self'; script-src has no unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval; the /docs CDN origin is included only when exposeApiDocs is true
regressionTests: apps/server/src/security-controls.test.ts :: responses carry a restrictive Content-Security-Policy
apps/server/src/security-controls.test.ts :: docs CDN origin is absent from CSP when API docs are disabled
Browser-verified: web app + dashboard driven under Chromium, 0 CSP violations, authenticated WebSocket OPEN
findings.residualRisk: style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' for Tailwind runtime styles.

findings.title: Unauthenticated analytics ingest had no rate limit and accepts client-chosen row keys
findings.attackerControlledInput: JSON body visitorId/sessionId plus unlimited request volume
findings.impact: Unbounded growth of analytics_sessions/events/vitals on the SQLite volume and pollution of dashboard aggregates
findings.remediation: Applied the existing rateLimit middleware to the whole analytics router at 240 requests / 10 min per resolved client address
regressionTests: apps/server/src/security-controls.test.ts :: unauthenticated analytics ingest is rate limited
findings.residualRisk: Server still trusts body-supplied visitorId/sessionId for the app platform, which has no cookie jar; a client can still fabricate its own identifiers within the rate budget.

findings.title: exposeApiDocs fails open when NODE_ENV is not exactly 'production'
findings.exploitability: Only if NODE_ENV is unset or misspelled in a production deployment
findings.impact: Full OpenAPI spec and Scalar UI exposed at /openapi.json and /docs
findings.remediation: Not changed. The shipped Dockerfile sets NODE_ENV=production (Dockerfile:31), so the deployed default is closed. Recommend inverting to an explicit opt-in.
findings.residualRisk: Any deployment path that does not go through this Dockerfile exposes docs by default.

findings.title: Login does not perform a dummy password verification for unknown usernames
findings.exploitability: Requires statistical timing measurement; argon2id makes the present/absent gap large
findings.remediation: Not changed. Recommend verifying against a fixed dummy hash when the user row is absent.
findings.residualRisk: GET /api/friends/search already discloses usernames to any authenticated user, so the marginal value of this leak is low.

rejected.subject: hono <4.12.34 (4 advisories)
rejected.evidence: Advisories cover CORS middleware, JSX memo() SSR, the proxy helper and language middleware. Grep across apps/server/src and packages found no use of hono/cors, hono/jsx, memo(), hono/proxy or languageDetector. Upgraded to 4.13.5 anyway as cheap hygiene.

rejected.subject: react-router RSC-mode CSRF bypass
rejected.evidence: apps/web and apps/dashboard are Vite SPAs; RSC mode is not enabled and there is no server-side react-router.

rejected.subject: image-size, js-yaml, brace-expansion, nanoid, postcss, fast-uri, uuid
rejected.evidence: All reach the tree through eslint/expo/jest/vite build tooling, not the server runtime. None sit on a request path.

rejected.subject: Path traversal in static file serving
rejected.evidence: apps/server/src/static.ts:61-62 decodes with decodeURIComponent BEFORE testing for '..', so %2e%2e is caught; WHATWG URL parsing already normalises literal ../ segments out of pathname. Ordering is correct.

rejected.subject: CSRF on admin state-changing routes
rejected.evidence: lc_admin_sess is SameSite=Lax and host-only, so it is not sent on cross-site POST; JSON-validated routes additionally require a Content-Type a simple form cannot set.

rejected.subject: SQL injection in dashboard list/sort queries
rejected.evidence: Every value is bound with ? placeholders. The only interpolated identifiers are sort/dir, narrowed to literal unions by ternaries at the route boundary (admin/routes.ts:226,271) before reaching the repos.

rejected.subject: SSRF via GeoIP updater and Insights fetch
rejected.evidence: Both target hardcoded MaxMind hosts. The Insights path additionally validates the IP with node:net isIP() in normalizeIp() before interpolation, and only the URL path can vary.

rejected.subject: IDOR on chat, images, push and friends
rejected.evidence: ChatService.requireMembership gates every conversation path; ImagesService.canAccess requires ownership or membership of a conversation the image was sent in; push/expo repos scope deletes by user_id; FriendsService.respond checks addressee_id. Image IDs are UUIDs.

rejected.subject: Service worker caching authenticated responses
rejected.evidence: apps/web/src/sw.ts only calls precacheAndRoute(self.__WB_MANIFEST) over build assets. No runtime caching strategy is registered, so no API response is cached.

rejected.subject: password matches in apps/server/src/**/*.test.ts and test/helpers.ts
rejected.evidence: All hits are the synthetic literal used by the test fixtures. Tracked apps/app/.env.* contain only EXPO_PUBLIC_* URLs, per the audit plan's known-benign list. Full-history scan across all reachable commits found no real credential.
